correctness.rationale: For arbitrary monitored F, the complete-graph two-fermion hopping has exactly two distinct eigenspaces. The monitored constraints turn these into component-constant potentials on F and cycle flows on the complement; a direct edge-incidence proof gives their orthogonal projector, all Betti/component ranks and the effective-resistance diagonal. Positive jump rates exclude any additional nondecaying bright eigenmode. Exact and numerical independently written scripts check projector entries and maximality on finite graph instances; all-size validity rests on the written proof.

value.rationale: An infinite-family graph-topological exact classification answers a physical detection-design problem: when patterned two-body loss on a complete network leaves perfect protection, what initial-pair survival remains, and how many channels are necessary for complete eventual capture. The dual obstructions, exact electrical-resistance law, and sharp detector-count threshold go beyond an isolated finite table or routine parameter relabeling.
